To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
evolved robots can be robust and resilient to damage and that evolved robots are more robust and resilient to morphological damage than robots designed by hand.

(1) evolved robots with morphologies found in nature are more robust than evolved robots with morphologically novel bodies; (2) evolved neural controllers are more robust than manually designed controllers; and (3) evolved neural controllers that use the same morphologies as evolved neural controllers are also more robust than manually constructed controllers.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the neural and morphologic subsystems of a machine are not interchangeable: the same neural architecture can be implemented in different morphologies and produce different adaptive behaviors, and the same morphology can be controlled by different neural architectures to produce different adaptive behaviors.
